sentences.text: Oceanotitan dantasi is a sauropod dinosaur genus known from the Upper Jurassic Lourinhã Formation in Portugal.
The genus is represented by a single specimen containing several tail vertebrae and appendicular bones.

Oceanotitan has unique features separating it from other macronarians, including a sagittal groove on the first tail vertebra, lateral depressions on tail vertebrae, and an elliptical concavity on the scapula.
The total body size of Oceanotitan is uncertain due to the lack of complete remains.

The holotype specimen, SHN 181, is stored at the Sociedade de História Natural in Torres Vedras, Portugal, after being found at the coastal cliffs of Praia de Valmitão in Lourinhã by a private collector.
The genus was formally described in 2019 by Pedro Mocho and colleagues.
The generic name Oceanotitan means "ocean giant" and refers to the Atlantic Ocean location and Greek mythology.
Oceanotitan is classified within the unranked family Titanosauriformes.
Oceanotitan dantasi lived during the Late Jurassic Kimmeridgian stage, approximately 152 million years ago, specifically between 152.21 and 149.2 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
Oceanotitan lived in a river system environment rather than a marine one.
The ecosystem where Oceanotitan lived had flora and fauna similar to those of the Morrison Formation and Tendaguru Formation.
Oceanotitan lived alongside various theropods, sauropods, a stegosaur, and an ornithopod.
